# dlaisnan

> Tests for NaN by comparing two arguments for inequality.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaisnan from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaisnan';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaisnan( din1, din2 ) → boolean
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `din1` | `number` | in |  |  | first value |
| `din2` | `number` | in |  |  | second value |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `din2`: Two numbers to compare for inequality.

</details>

**Returns** `boolean`: result

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaisnan.ndarray( din1, din2 ) → boolean
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `din1` | `number` | in |  |  | first value |
| `din2` | `number` | in |  |  | second value |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `din2`: Two numbers to compare for inequality.

</details>

**Returns** `boolean`: true if din1 !== din2

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

## Notes

-   `dlaisnan()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAISNAN`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlaisnan.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import dlaisnan from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaisnan';

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dlaisnan( 1, 1 );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dlaisnan.ndarray( 1, 1 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAISNAN`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

This routine is not for general use. It exists solely to avoid over-optimization in DISNAN.

DLAISNAN checks for NaNs by comparing its two arguments for inequality. NaN is the only floating-point value where NaN != NaN returns .TRUE. To check for NaNs, pass the same variable as both arguments.

A compiler must assume that the two arguments are not the same variable, and the test will not be optimized away. Interprocedural or whole-program optimization may delete this test. The ISNAN functions will be replaced by the correct Fortran 03 intrinsic once the intrinsic is widely available.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
